title: Sequence-length Forecast Kernel Adapter (seqlen predictor + kernel mapping)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce prefill+decode P50/P95 latency and token cost by selecting the optimal implementation path at RPC ingress using a lightweight sequence-length predictor and an offline kernel mapping table. The adapter should avoid per-request microprobes in steady state while preserving safety (fallback to robust kernels) and enabling fast online adaptation via bandit-style signals.

Background: Current runtime uses a combination of microprobes and static heuristics to select kernels. Microprobes add extra latency and variance; static heuristics fail to capture bursty seqlen distributions and model-version/hardware interactions. A small predictor that runs at the edge of the request path (CPU) can forecast a distribution over expected output lengths given prompt metadata + first token/window and pick a kernel path tuned for that range. An offline autotuner will periodically recompute kernel mappings per (model-version, quantization, arch) using microbenchmarks and a cost-latency objective.

Approach:
1) Implement a "seqlen predictor" service that takes: model id, prompt metadata (system/instruction flags), first-k tokens summary (hashed/embedding), and returns a seqlen percentile vector (p50/p90/p99) and confidence. Predictor MUST be extremely small (<=300KB compiled) and sub-millisecond at 3GHz CPU.
2) Build a Kernel Mapping Table (KMT) artifact keyed by (model-version, quant-profile, arch-tag, seqlen-bucket) produced by offline autotuner. KMT entries map to kernel implementation ids (e.g., attn-fused-16b, attn-block-32b, kv-skip-quant) and preferred scheduler hints (batching window, prefill vs decode split).
3) Runtime adapter integrates predictor + KMT: on request ingress, call predictor, map to a kernel id from KMT; if confidence low or KMT missing, fallback to conservative kernel and enqueue a low-priority microprobe to update KMT for that key.
4) Offline autotuner: run batched microbenchmarks across a matrix of sequence lengths, batch sizes, and archs. Use Bayesian optimizer to fit a cost function (latency+token-cost penalty) and emit KMT. Maintain historical performance traces to detect drift and trigger re-tuning.
5) Online feedback: collect per-request latency/cost and use a lightweight exponential-weighted-bandit per key to adjust selection frequency for exploration.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end P95 latency for prefill reduced by >=10% for 90% of traffic in initial canary.
- Token cost reduced by >=6% on mixed seqlen workloads without increasing P99 latency.
- Predictor inference adds <0.5ms median overhead at 3GHz CPU and <2ms p99.
- KMT lookup adds negligible overhead; offline autotuner runs within daily maintenance window and converges for top 50 models.

Out-of-scope for MVP: full multi-GPU scheduling changes, per-token kernel switching during decode (we only select prefill+initial decode policy).

Security/privacy: Predictor inputs must avoid sending user content to external services. First-k token summaries are hashed/quantized embeddings only; ensure no reversible transformations. KMT artifacts are stored in S3 with customer and region scoping for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Rollout plan:
- Spike/prototype (2w): implement CPU predictor prototype + toy KMT and end-to-end path locally.
- Microbench/autotuner (3w): microbench suite + Bayesian optimizer integration.
- Canary (2w): small percentage of hosted traffic with logging and fail-safes.
- Gradual ramp (4w): increase coverage, monitor metrics, iterate.

Metrics to monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency prefill & decode, tokens per request, cost-per-1000-tokens, predictor latency/cpu%, failure/fallback rate, KMT staleness, exploration overhead.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/seq-len-kernel-adapter (WIP)
- Microbench harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-microbench/tree/seqlen-adapter
- Initial notebooks: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/u/0/folders/seqlen-adapter-experiments

Risks:
- Predictor mispredictions causing suboptimal kernel choice could temporarily increase P99; mitigated via confidence thresholds and conservative fallback.
- Autotuner cost/time: full sweep across archs is expensive; prioritize top-traffic models and use warm-starts.
- Data drift with new quant profiles or kernels; schedule weekly sanity rechecks and create alerts for KMT regressions.

Next milestones:
- 2025-02-21: CPU predictor prototype + unit tests.
- 2025-03-03: offline autotuner accepts input matrix and produces KMT for two internal models.
- 2025-03-10: runtime adapter integrated in staging + end-to-end microbench.

Notes: This ticket focuses on the selection/adaptation layer and the offline mapping. Separate tickets will cover in-depth scheduler changes and multi-GPU allocations once KMT is mature.
